key_insight: A moving generalized vertical coordinate lets a nonhydrostatic unstructured-grid ocean model switch between z-level, terrain-following, isopycnal, and hybrid layers to better resolve complex 3D flows like internal solitary waves.
engineering_relevance: This improves practical coastal and ocean simulation fidelity on realistic geometries while preserving conservative, positivity-safe numerics on horizontally unstructured meshes.
method: Integrated a generalized vertical coordinate (GVC) into the SUNTANS nonhydrostatic, C-grid ocean model.
Added a conservative momentum advection scheme tailored to unstructured grids.
Implemented a positivity-preserving layer-height update for stable hybrid vertical coordinates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on turbulent channel flow and comparative simulations of internal solitary waves with associated bottom boundary-layer instability to demonstrate the hybrid coordinate advantages.
watch_item: The added coordinate-moving and layer-height machinery increases implementation complexity and requires careful stability/positivity handling on unstructured grids.
paper_title: An unstructured-grid, nonhydrostatic, GVC ocean model Part I: Model description and application of vertical hybrid coordinates to internal solitary waves
